name: terminal_spawn
description: Starts a long-running command (dev server, watcher, test runner) in the background and returns its process_id, pid, status, whether it is ready and a log cursor. Optionally waits until it is ready (a port accepts connections, an http:// URL answers 200, or a regex matches its output). Read output with terminal_logs, stop it with terminal_signal. The process ends with the session.

name.description: Optional label shown in status listings.

cwd.description: Working directory inside the workspace (default: the workspace root).

env.description: Extra environment variables for this process only.

tty.description: Reserved: pseudo-terminals are not supported yet.

url.description: kind=http: plain http:// URL that must answer 200.

pattern.description: kind=log: regular expression matched against the output.

timeout_ms.description: Give up waiting after this long (default 30000, max 600000).

name: terminal_logs
description: Reads the output of a process started with terminal_spawn (or Bash run_in_background) after a cursor. Returns the text followed by a line with the process state and the cursor to pass next time. Optionally keep only lines matching a regular expression.

cursor.description: Cursor from a previous call (default: from the start).

filter.description: Optional regular expression: only matching lines are returned.

name: terminal_signal
description: Sends a signal (int, term or kill) to a process started with terminal_spawn; the whole process tree is signalled.

name: terminal_status
description: Shows the state of one process, or lists all processes of this session when process_id is omitted.
